subject: Multi-team burst capacity, new projects and term clarification
messages:
From: Jordan Hayes <jordan@luminahq.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@luminahq.com
Date: 2026-11-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Expanding to 4 more squads — capacity needs & term questions

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re ready to move forward with expansion but there are two quick asks from our platform and legal teams:

1) We’ll be adding four new internal projects (two analytics, two patient-facing search endpoints). Can you confirm per-hour token throughput we should reserve and what the pricing delta looks like for burst capacity?

2) Our procurement team wants to understand how adding new projects mid-term affects our existing 12-month commitment and whether we can push some of the new usage into a trial credit or pilot bucket while we validate latency under load.

I attached a simple project list (names + projected Q1 traffic). Can we get a quick plan + rough timeline before EOD Monday? We’re aiming to coordinate onboarding across engineering and security.

Appreciate it — Jordan
Lumina Health

Attachments: Lumina_Project_List.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <jordan@luminahq.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Expanding to 4 more squads — capacity needs & term questions

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear ask and for the project list. Quick answers up front, then a proposed MAP.

- Burst capacity: based on the traffic estimates you sent, we recommend reserving a baseline pool for the two patient-facing endpoints (~1000 requests/min peak, ~30M tokens/day combined) and a smaller pool for analytics (burst to 500 req/min). I’ll put exact GPU-hour and token-rate numbers below after Ben confirms kernel/quantization choices.

- Term/commit: adding new projects doesn’t automatically extend the 12-month term. We can:
  * Option A — absorb a portion of early-stage validation into a 90-day pilot credit (we’ll allocate pilot tokens from your committed bucket and report usage separately), or
  * Option B — add the new projects under the existing commitment and prorate the pricing for the remainder of the term.

Proposed next steps (MAP):
  1) Ben to confirm recommended instance types + estimated reserved throughput.
  2) Technical kickoff (1-hour) to align on auth/keys and KV cache needs.
  3) Create two short-lived API keys for pilot projects; production keys activated after validation.
  4) Legal runs the SOW addendum for the pricing route you pick.

I’m looping Ben (serving/runtime) and Laura (eng-svc lead on contracts) on details. Can you confirm which option (A or B) procurement prefers?

Thanks — Olga
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T12:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Expanding to 4 more squads — capacity needs & term questions

Olga / Laura — quick tech read on Jordan’s projections:

- For the two patient-facing endpoints (low-latency requirement), I recommend a mix of 2x A100-class reservations with auto-burst to dedicated spot capacity for traffic spikes. That will cover ~40M tokens/day sustained with headroom; continuous batching and prefix caching should keep p95 under 220ms for short prompts.

- Analytics projects: medium-priority; we can route them to a lower-cost quantized runtime (4-bit) with slower p95 (~480ms) but significantly lower unit cost.

Estimated monthly delta if added to existing commitment (ballpark):
  * Patient-facing pool add: +$18,000/mo
  * Analytics pool add: +$6,500/mo
  * Pilot credit (90d) option: one-time credit of ~$25,000 (applied against committed usage if you convert to Option B).

I’ll draft a short capacity spec and a JSON example of key-per-project namespacing (for the kickoff). Also: we can issue two pilot API keys and limit them to project namespaces.

—Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <jordan@luminahq.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, contracts@luminahq.com
Date: 2026-11-09T08:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Expanding to 4 more squads — capacity needs & term questions

Jordan — following up with the concrete MAP and attached draft SOW addendum. Short answers to your procurement question:

- If you want to validate before committing (Option A), we’ll provision two pilot keys and a pilot pool. Pilot runs 90 days; if you convert to full production during that window we’ll credit $25k against the committed spend.

- If you prefer a clean addition to the existing commitment (Option B), we’ll prorate pricing for the remaining term and increase your reserved GPU pool immediately; that triggers a minor amendment to the SOW.

Key dates (proposed):
  * 11/10 — technical kickoff (1-hr) with Lumina eng + Redwood SEs
  * 11/11-11/24 — pilot window (if Option A) or immediate provisioning (Option B)
  * 12/01 — production keys activated / SLOs confirmed

Please find the SOW draft attached and a short project list we received from you. If procurement prefers Option A, confirm and I’ll have contracts generate the credit memo and pilot key bundle.

Thanks — Olga

Attachments: Lumina_MAP_v1.pdf, SOW_Lumina_draft.docx
From: contracts@luminahq.com
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Expanding to 4 more squads — capacity needs & term questions

Hi Olga / Laura — thanks for the options. Procurement reviewed both and prefers Option A (90-day pilot with credit) so we can validate latency and data-flow before committing more of the annual spend. A few clarifying asks for the SOW addendum:

1) Please add language that pilot usage up to $25k will not count against current monthly billing and that credits apply only if Lumina elects to convert projects to production within 90 days.
2) We need a short data retention line for cached prefixes (max 30 days) and confirmation that no patient PII will be logged in shared telemetry.
3) Can you provide a timeline for issuing the two pilot API keys and the onboarding checklist for our infra team?

If you can update the SOW with these points, we’ll route the addendum through our legal and aim to sign within 5 business days.

Regards,
Procurement Team — Lumina Health
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <jordan@luminahq.com>, contracts@luminahq.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Expanding to 4 more squads — capacity needs & term questions

Thanks — confirmed. Action items and owners below:

1) Contracts (Laura) to update SOW addendum with pilot credit language + retention clause (due 11/11 EOD).
2) Ben to finalize the capacity spec and instance recommendation + a namespaced API key naming example (shared 11/10 EOD).
3) Olga to provision two pilot API keys scoped to the project namespaces and share onboarding checklist (keys + checklist shared 11/11 AM).

Tentative kickoff: 11/10 10:00 AM PT — meeting invite will be sent after Laura confirms SOW language.

Jordan — if that timeline works, I’ll queue the pilot keys and notify your infra contact once they’re created. Appreciate the quick turnaround from procurement.

Best — Olga
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: SOW_Lumina_draft.docx (will be updated), Lumina_MAP_v1.pdf, Lumina_Project_List.xlsx
